title.zh: 卷一百二十六 列傳第七十六: 李揆 李涵 陳少游 盧鸑 裴諝
title.en: Volume 126 Biographies 76: Li Kui, Li Han, Chen Shaoyou, Lu Yue, Pei Xu
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 列傳第七十六: 李揆 李涵 陳少游 盧鸑 裴諝 Volume 126 Biographies 76: Li Kui, Li Han, Chen Shaoyou, Lu Yue, Pei Xu

sentences.zh: 李揆字端卿，隴西成紀人，而家於鄭州，代為冠族。

translations.literal: Li Kui, style name Duanging, was a man of Chengji in Longxi, but his family resided in Zhengzhou; for generations they were a foremost clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, whose courtesy name was Duanging, came from Chengji in Longxi, though his family had settled in Zhengzhou as a leading clan for generations.

sentences.zh: 秦府學士、給事中玄道玄孫，秘書監、贈吏部尚書成裕之子。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Xuan Daoxuan, Academician of the Qin Prince's household and Recipient of Memorials, and the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat and posthumously bestowed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Xuan Daoxuan, who had served as an academician in the Qin prince's household and as a supervising censor, and from Chengyu, director of the Secretariat and posthumously honored as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and fond of study, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and studious, with a gift for writing.

sentences.zh: 開元末，舉進士，補陳留尉，獻書闕下，詔中書試文章，擢拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Chenliu district captain, presented a book at court, and by imperial order the Secretariat tested his writings and promoted him to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyuan reign he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed district captain of Chenliu, and submitted a work to the throne; the emperor ordered the Secretariat to examine his writing and then appointed him right reminder.

sentences.zh: 改右補闕、起居郎，知宗子表疏。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Supplementation Censor and Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and was charged with imperial-clan memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made right supplementation censor and attendant of the heir apparent, with responsibility for memorials from the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 遷司勛員外郎、考功郎中，並知制誥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Merit section and Director in the Examination section, and concurrently drafted imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director in the ministry of personnel's merit office and director in its examination office, while also drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 扈從劍南，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Jiannan and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When the court withdrew to Jiannan he accompanied the emperor and was appointed a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era he was additionally Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan reign he also served as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 揆嘗以主司取士，多不考實，徒峻其堤防，索其書策，殊未知藝不至者，文史之囿亦不能摛詞，深昧求賢之意也。

translations.literal: Kui once observed that chief examiners in selecting scholars often did not verify substance, merely heightening barriers and demanding written answers, utterly failing to know that when talent does not reach the mark even the domain of letters and histories cannot produce words—deeply contrary to the intent of seeking worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Kui had once remarked that examination commissioners often failed to test real ability, tightening procedural barriers and demanding written answers instead, without recognizing that candidates who lacked genuine talent could not compose even within the fields of letters and history—thus betraying the true purpose of seeking able men.

sentences.zh: 其試進士文章，請於庭中設《五經》、諸史及《切韻》本於床，而引貢士謂之曰：「大國選士，但務得者，經籍在此，請恣尋檢。

translations.literal: For the jinshi literary examination he requested that copies of the Five Classics, various histories, and the Qieyun be set on couches in the courtyard, and led the candidates forward, saying: "A great state selects scholars and seeks only those who can succeed; the classics are here—please search and consult as you wish."
translations.idiomatic: For the jinshi literary examination he had copies of the Five Classics, various histories, and the rhyme dictionary placed on tables in the courtyard, then addressed the candidates: "In selecting scholars a great state cares only for true ability; the texts are here—consult them freely."

sentences.zh: 」由是數月之間，美聲上聞，未及畢事，遷中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿崇文館大學士、修國史。

translations.literal: " Within a few months his fine reputation reached the throne; before the examinations were finished he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, Grand Academician of the Jixian and Chongwen Halls, and compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months his reputation reached the emperor. Before the examinations ended he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, grand councillor, grand academician of the Jixian and Chongwen halls, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 揆美風儀，善奏對，每有敷陳，皆符獻替。

translations.literal: Kui had fine bearing and was skilled at audience responses; whenever he presented counsel it accorded with the principle of offering and replacing.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was distinguished in appearance and eloquent in audience, and his policy recommendations consistently hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 肅宗賞嘆之，嘗謂揆曰：「卿門地、人物、文章，皆當代所推。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong admired and praised him, once saying to Kui: "Your lineage, person, and writings are all esteemed in the age."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong admired him and once told him, "Your family standing, personal qualities, and literary talent are all unrivaled in our time."

sentences.zh: 」故進人稱為三絕。

translations.literal: " Therefore people at court called him the Triple Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers accordingly called him the "triple excellence."

sentences.zh: 其為舍人也，宗室請加張皇后「翊聖」之號，肅宗召揆問之，對曰；

translations.literal: When he was a drafter, members of the imperial clan requested that the title "Assistant Sage" be added for Empress Zhang; Suzong summoned Kui to inquire, and he replied:
translations.idiomatic: While serving as a Secretariat drafter, he was asked when the imperial clan sought to add the honorific "Assistant Sage" for Empress Zhang. The emperor summoned Kui for his view, and he answered:

sentences.zh: 「臣觀往古后妃，終則有謚。

translations.literal: "Your servant observes that in antiquity empresses and consorts, when they ended, received posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity, empresses and consorts received posthumous titles only after death.

sentences.zh: 生加尊號，未之前聞。

translations.literal: Adding honorific titles during life has never been heard of before.
translations.idiomatic: Bestowing honorific titles during one's lifetime was unheard of.

sentences.zh: 景龍失政，韋氏專恣，加號翊聖，今若加皇后之號，與韋氏同。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era government failed, the Wei clan acted with unchecked arrogance, and the title Assistant Sage was added; if the empress is given such a title now, it is the same as with the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During the failed Jinglong reign Empress Wei dominated the court and took the title Assistant Sage; to grant the empress the same title now would repeat that precedent.

sentences.zh: 陛下明聖，動遵典禮，豈可蹤景龍故事哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is enlightened and sagely, always following canonical ritual—how could you follow the Jinglong precedent!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is enlightened and observant of ritual propriety—how could you follow the Jinglong precedent!

sentences.zh: 」肅宗驚曰：「凡才幾誤我家事。

translations.literal: " Suzong said in alarm: "Mediocre talent nearly ruined my household affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed in alarm, "Mediocre advisers nearly ruined my house."

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: " and the matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時代宗自廣平王改封成王，張皇后有子數歲，陰有奪宗之議。

translations.literal: At that time Daizong had been changed from Prince of Guangping to Prince of Cheng; Empress Zhang had a son of several years, and there was a secret plan to seize the succession.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Daizong had been renamed from Prince of Guangping to Prince of Cheng, while Empress Zhang had a young son and secretly schemed to displace the heir.

sentences.zh: 揆因對見，肅宗從容曰：「成王嫡長有功，今當命嗣，卿意何如？

translations.literal: When Kui was received in audience, Suzong said at ease: "The Prince of Cheng is the eldest legitimate son and has merit; he should now be named heir—what is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: On another audience Kui was received, and the emperor said casually, "Prince Cheng is the legitimate eldest son and has earned merit; it is time to name him heir. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」揆拜賀曰：「陛下言及於此，社稷之福，天下幸甚，臣不勝大慶。

translations.literal: " Kui bowed in congratulation and said: "When Your Majesty speaks to this point, it is the fortune of the altars of state; the realm is greatly blessed; your servant cannot contain his great rejoicing."
translations.idiomatic: Kui bowed in congratulation and said, "When Your Majesty speaks thus, it is the fortune of the realm; all under Heaven will rejoice, and your servant is overwhelmed with gratitude."

sentences.zh: 」肅宗喜曰：「朕計決矣。

translations.literal: " Suzong said with pleasure: "My decision is settled."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with satisfaction, "My mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 」自此頗承恩遇，遂蒙大用。

translations.literal: " From this he received considerable favor and was soon greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he enjoyed the emperor's favor and rose to great power.

sentences.zh: 時京師多盜賊，有通衢殺人置溝中者，李輔國方恣橫，上請選羽林騎士五百人以備巡檢。

translations.literal: At that time the capital had many bandits; there were cases of killing on main roads and casting bodies into ditches. Li Fuguo was then acting with unchecked arrogance and requested that five hundred Imperial Guard horsemen be selected for patrol inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in the capital, with murders on main thoroughfares and bodies dumped in ditches. Li Fuguo, then at the height of his power, asked that five hundred Imperial Guard cavalry be assigned to patrol duty.

sentences.zh: 揆上疏曰：「昔西漢以南北軍相攝，故周勃因南軍入北軍，遂安劉氏。

translations.literal: Kui submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly the Western Han used the Northern and Southern Armies to restrain each other; therefore Zhou Bo, through the Southern Army entering the Northern Army, was able to secure the Liu house."
translations.idiomatic: Kui submitted a memorial: "In the Western Han the northern and southern armies were meant to check each other; that was how Zhou Bo, by turning the southern army against the northern, saved the Liu dynasty."

sentences.zh: 皇朝置南北衙，文武區分，以相伺察。

translations.literal: Our dynasty established the Northern and Southern Bureaus, separating civil and military, to observe each other.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty likewise divided the northern and southern bureaus, separating civil and military authority so each could watch the other.

sentences.zh: 今以羽林代金吾警夜，忽有非常之變，將何以制之？

translations.literal: Now to replace the Gold Crow guards' night watch with the Imperial Guard—if a sudden extraordinary change occurs, how will it be controlled?
translations.idiomatic: If the Imperial Guard replaces the Gold Crow guards for night patrol, how will we control a sudden emergency?

sentences.zh: 」遂制罷羽林之請。

translations.literal: " and by edict the Imperial Guard request was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict rejecting the Imperial Guard proposal.

sentences.zh: 揆在相位，決事獻替，雖甚博辨，性銳於名利，深為物議所非。

translations.literal: When Kui held the chancellorship, in deciding affairs he offered and replaced counsel; though very broad in debate, his nature was sharp toward fame and profit, and he was deeply criticized in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Kui was learned and forceful in debate, yet he was fiercely ambitious and widely criticized.

sentences.zh: 又其兄皆自有時名，滯於冗官，竟不引進。

translations.literal: Moreover his elder brothers all had reputations in their time but were stuck in superfluous posts; he never advanced them.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers were men of established reputation, yet he left them mired in minor posts and never promoted them.

sentences.zh: 同列呂諲，地望雖懸，政事在揆之右，罷相，自賓客為荊南節度，聲問甚美。

translations.literal: His colleague Lü Yin, though their standing was far apart, in government affairs stood above Kui; dismissed from the chancellorship, he went from guest to Jingnan military commissioner, and his reputation was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Lü Yin, though of far lower birth, had outranked him in office. After leaving the chancellorship Lü served as military commissioner of Jingnan and won an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 懼其重入，遂密令直省至諲管內抅求諲過失。

translations.literal: Fearing his return to power, he secretly ordered direct secretariat staff to go within Yin's jurisdiction and seek out Yin's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Yin might return to court, he secretly sent secretariat staff into Yin's jurisdiction to hunt for faults.

sentences.zh: 諲密疏自陳，乃貶揆萊州長史同正員，其制旨曰：「扇湖南之八州，沮江陵之節制。

translations.literal: Yin submitted a secret memorial in his own defense, and Kui was demoted to Senior Administrator of Laizhou with the same-rank stipend; the edict read: "He fanned the eight prefectures south of the lake and obstructed Jiangling's military control."
translations.idiomatic: Yin submitted a secret memorial in his own defense, and Kui was demoted to senior administrator of Laizhou on reduced stipend. The edict charged him with "stirring the eight prefectures south of the lake and obstructing Jiangling's military control."

sentences.zh: 」揆既黜官，數日，其兄皆改授為司門員外郎。

translations.literal: " After Kui was removed from office, within days his brothers were all reassigned as vice directors in the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of Kui's dismissal his brothers were all reassigned to minor posts in the gate office.

sentences.zh: 後累年，揆量移歙州刺史。

translations.literal: After several years Kui was transferred by quota to Shezhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to prefect of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 初，揆秉政，侍中苗晉卿累薦元載為重官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kui held power, Chief Minister Miao Jinqing repeatedly recommended Yuan Zai for weighty office.
translations.idiomatic: While Kui was in power, chief minister Miao Jinqing had repeatedly recommended Yuan Zai for high office.

sentences.zh: 揆自恃門望，以載地寒，意甚輕易，不納，而謂晉卿曰：「龍章鳳姿之士不見用，麞頭鼠目之子乃求官。

translations.literal: Kui relied on his lineage prestige; because Zai's origins were humble he treated him very lightly and did not accept him, saying to Jinqing: "Men of dragon markings and phoenix bearing are not employed, while sons with deer heads and rat eyes seek office."
translations.idiomatic: Kui, trusting in his pedigree, looked down on Zai's humble origins and refused the recommendation, telling Jinqing, "Men of true nobility go unused, while creatures with deer heads and rat eyes beg for posts."

sentences.zh: 」載銜恨頗深。

translations.literal: " Zai harbored deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zai nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 及載登相位，因揆當徙職，遂奏為試秘書監，江淮養疾。

translations.literal: When Zai reached the chancellorship, because Kui was due to be transferred in office, he memorialized that he be made provisional Director of the Secretariat to recuperate from illness in the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai became chief minister he used Kui's scheduled transfer to have him appointed provisional director of the Secretariat to recuperate in the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 既無祿俸，家復貧乏，孀孤百口，丐食取給。

translations.literal: He had no salary stipend, and his household was again impoverished; widows and orphans numbering a hundred mouths begged for food to sustain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Without salary and with a household of more than a hundred widows and orphans, the family lived by begging.

sentences.zh: 萍寄諸州，凡十五六年，其牧守稍薄，則又移居，故其遷徙者，蓋十余州焉。

translations.literal: He drifted among the prefectures for altogether fifteen or sixteen years; when a prefect or governor was somewhat cold, he moved again, so the places to which he relocated numbered more than ten prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For fifteen or sixteen years he drifted from prefecture to prefecture, moving on whenever a local governor grew unfriendly—altogether more than ten jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 元載以罪誅，除揆睦州刺史，入拜國子祭酒、禮部尚書，為盧杞所惡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai was executed for crime, Kui was appointed Muzhou prefect; he entered court as Chancellor of the National University and Minister of Rites, and was hated by Lu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Zai was executed for treason, Kui was appointed prefect of Muzhou, then recalled as chancellor of the national university and minister of rites, but was detested by Lu Qi.

sentences.zh: 德宗在山南，令充入蕃會盟使，加左僕射。

translations.literal: When Dezong was in Shannan he was ordered to serve as envoy for entering the barbarians to conclude alliance, and was additionally made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was at Shannan, Kui was ordered to serve as envoy to the Tibetans for a peace alliance and was made left vice director.

sentences.zh: 行至鳳州，以疾卒，興元元年四月也，年七十四。

translations.literal: Reaching Fengzhou he died of illness, in the fourth month of the first year of Xingyuan, at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Fengzhou and died of illness in the fourth month of 784, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，喪事官給。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, and funeral affairs were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as minister of works, with state provision for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 李涵，高平王道立曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Han was the great-grandson of Li Daoli, Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han was the great-grandson of Li Daoli, Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 父少康，宋州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shaokang was Songzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaokang had served as prefect of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 涵簡素恭慎，有名宗室，累授贊善大夫、兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Han was plain, respectful, and cautious, a noted member of the imperial clan, and was repeatedly appointed Companion to the Heir Apparent and concurrently Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Han was plain, respectful, and cautious, a noted prince of the blood, and was repeatedly appointed companion to the heir apparent and attending censor.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度郭子儀奏為關內鹽池判官。

translations.literal: Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi memorialized him as salt-pond judge within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, recommended him as salt-pond administrator for the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 肅宗北幸平涼，未有所適。

translations.literal: When Suzong went north to Pingliang he had not yet decided where to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong withdrew north to Pingliang the court had not yet chosen a destination.

sentences.zh: 涵與朔方留後杜鴻漸，草箋具朔方兵馬招集之勢，軍資倉儲庫物之數，鹹推涵宗枝之英，純厚忠信，乃令涵奉箋至平涼謁見。

translations.literal: Han and Shuofang acting commissioner Du Hongjian drafted a memorial detailing the situation of Shuofang troops and horses being gathered, and the numbers of military supplies, storehouses, and treasury goods; all praised Han as an outstanding branch of the imperial clan, pure, thick, loyal, and trustworthy, and so Han was ordered to present the memorial at Pingliang for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Du Hongjian, acting commissioner of Shuofang, drafted a memorial detailing Shuofang's military strength and stores of supplies. All praised Han as an outstanding member of the imperial clan, pure and loyal, and he was sent to present the memorial to the emperor at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 涵敷奏明辯，動合事機，肅宗大悅，除右司員外郎，累至司封郎中、宗正少卿。

translations.literal: Han presented his memorial with clarity and persuasiveness, and his motions fit the moment; Suzong was greatly pleased and appointed him Vice Director in the Right Secretariat, then in succession Director in the Enfeoffment section and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Han presented his report with clarity and sound judgment, greatly pleasing the emperor, who appointed him vice director in the right secretariat and later director in the enfeoffment office and vice director of the imperial clan court.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，初平河朔，代宗以涵忠謹洽聞，遷左庶子、兼御史中丞、河北宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, when the Hebei region was first pacified, Daizong because Han was known for loyalty, prudence, and broad repute transferred him to Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Hebei consolation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 762, when the Hebei region was first pacified, Daizong appointed him left guardian of the heir apparent, censor-in-chief, and Hebei consolation commissioner in recognition of his loyalty and reputation.

sentences.zh: 會丁母憂，起復本官而行，每州縣郵驛，公事之外，未嘗啟口，疏飯飲水，席地而息。

translations.literal: He happened to enter mourning for his mother, but was recalled to his former office and set out; at every prefecture and district post station, apart from public business he never opened his mouth, ate plain rice and drank water, and slept on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning to resume the mission. At every post station he spoke only on official business, ate plain food, drank water, and slept on the ground.

sentences.zh: 使還，請罷官終喪制，代宗以其毀瘠，許之。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he requested to leave office and complete the mourning rites; Daizong because of his emaciation from grief granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he asked to resign and complete mourning; Daizong, seeing how grief had wasted him, granted the request.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除給事中，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Supervising Censor and transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was made supervising censor and then left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以幽州之亂，充河朔宣慰使。

translations.literal: Because of the turmoil in Youzhou he was made Hebei-Shuofang consolation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion in Youzhou he served as Hebei consolation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大歷六年正月，為蘇州刺史、兼御史大夫，充浙江西道都團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Dali he was made Suzhou prefect, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and commissioned as overall training-and-observation commissioner of the Zhejiang West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 771 he was appointed prefect of Suzhou, censor-in-chief, and overall training-and-observation commissioner of the Zhejiang West circuit.

sentences.zh: 十一年，來朝，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he came to court and was appointed Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 776 he came to court and was appointed chief censor.

sentences.zh: 京畿觀察使李棲筠歿，代之。

translations.literal: Capital-region observation commissioner Li Qiyun died, and Han replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of the capital region, died, Han succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，以涵和易，無剸割之才，除太子少傅，充山陵副使。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, because Han was mild and easy and lacked the talent for decisive cutting, he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne he judged Han too mild for decisive leadership and made him junior tutor of the heir apparent and deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 涵判官殿中侍御史呂渭上言：「涵父名少康，今官名犯諱，恐乖禮典。

translations.literal: Han's aide, Palace Attending Censor Lü Wei, submitted a statement: "Han's father's name is Shaokang; the present office title violates taboo and may depart from ritual canon."
translations.idiomatic: Han's aide, palace attending censor Lü Wei, submitted: "Vice Director Han's father was named Shaokang; Han's present title violates naming taboo and may breach ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 」宰相崔祐甫奏曰：「若朝廷事有乖舛，群臣悉能如此，實太平之道。

translations.literal: " Chief Minister Cui Youfu memorialized: "If matters at court have errors and all ministers can act thus, it is truly the way of great peace."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Cui Youfu replied, "If every minister spoke up whenever court affairs went astray, that would be the way to true peace."

sentences.zh: 」除渭司門員外郎。

translations.literal: " Wei was appointed Vice Director in the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was promoted to vice director in the gate office.

sentences.zh: 尋有人言：「涵昔為宗正少卿，此時無言，今為少傅，妄有奏議。

translations.literal: Soon someone said: "Han formerly was Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court; at that time he said nothing; now as Junior Tutor he rashly has memorials."
translations.idiomatic: Soon critics noted that Han had held the post of vice director of the imperial clan court without raising the taboo issue, and now as junior tutor his aide had made a spurious objection.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「呂渭僭陳章奏，為其本使薄訴官名。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Lü Wei presumptuously submitted a memorial, making a slight complaint about an office title on behalf of his immediate superior."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Lü Wei presumptuously submitted a memorial, making a petty complaint about his superior's title."

sentences.zh: 朕以宋有司城之嫌，晉有詞曹之諱，嘆其忠於所事，亦謂確以上聞。

translations.literal: We took the Song case of the Minister of Works' taboo and the Jin case of the Documents Office taboo, and admired his loyalty to his charge, also deeming it firm in reporting upward.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling the Song taboo on the minister of works and the Jin taboo on the documents office, We admired his loyalty to his superior and thought his report conscientious.

sentences.zh: 乃加殊恩，俾膺厚賞。

translations.literal: We therefore added special favor and let him receive a rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore granted him special favor and a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 近聞所陳「少」字，往歲已任少卿，昔是今非，罔我何甚！

translations.literal: Recently hearing the "shao" character he cited—years ago he already held the post of Vice Director—what was then acceptable is now wrong; how greatly he has deceived Us!
translations.idiomatic: We now learn that the character shao in his complaint applied years ago when Han was already vice director—what was acceptable then is objectionable now. How greatly he has deceived Us!

sentences.zh: 豈得謬當朝典，更廁周行，宜佐遐籓，用誡薄俗。

translations.literal: How can he wrongly occupy court canon and again stand in the court ranks? He should assist a distant frontier commandery to admonish shallow custom.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot rightly remain in central office or court ranks; let him serve in a distant prefecture as a warning to shallow opportunists.

sentences.zh: 可歙州司馬同正。

translations.literal: He may be made Shezhou Vice Military Administrator with the same-rank stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to vice military administrator of Shezhou on reduced stipend.

sentences.zh: 」由是改涵為檢校工部尚書、兼光祿卿，仍充山陵副使。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Han was changed to Provisional Minister of Works, concurrently Director of the Imperial Household, still serving as deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Han was reassigned as provisional minister of works and director of the imperial household, while retaining his post as deputy tomb commissioner.

sentences.zh: 無幾，以右僕射致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he retired as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 興元元年九月卒，追贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Xingyuan he died, and was posthumously made Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of 784 and was posthumously honored as grand protector of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊，博州人也。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou was a man of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou came from Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 祖儼，安西副都護。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was Vice Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had served as vice protector-general of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 父慶，右武衛兵曹參軍，以少遊累贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Qing was a staff officer in the Right Martial Guard; because of Shaoyou he was repeatedly posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing had been a staff officer in the right martial guard and was posthumously honored as minister of works through Shaoyou's promotions.

sentences.zh: 少遊幼聰辯，初習《莊》、《列》、《老子》，為崇玄館學生，眾推引講經。

translations.literal: Shaoyou in youth was clever and eloquent; he first studied the Zhuangzi, Liezi, and Laozi, was a student of the Chongxuan Hall, and the crowd recommended him to expound the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou was clever and articulate as a youth. He studied the Zhuangzi, Liezi, and Laozi as a student of the Chongxuan Hall, and his fellows chose him to lecture on the classics.

sentences.zh: 時同列有私習經義者，期升坐日相問難。

translations.literal: At that time some of his peers had privately studied classic meanings and set the day of ascending the seat to question and challenge each other.
translations.idiomatic: Some classmates had privately studied the classics and planned to challenge him when he took the lectern.

sentences.zh: 及會，少遊攝齊升坐，音韻清辯，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: When they met, Shaoyou gathered his robes and ascended the seat; his tones were clear and his debate keen, and onlookers fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came he ascended the lectern with composed bearing, his voice clear and his argument sharp, drawing every eye in the hall.

sentences.zh: 所引文句，悉兼他義，諸生不能對，甚為大學士陳希烈所嘆賞，又以同宗，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: The passages he cited all combined other meanings; the students could not reply, and he was greatly admired by Grand Academician Chen Xilie, who because they shared the same clan treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Every passage he cited carried layered meanings, and none of the students could answer. Grand academician Chen Xilie greatly admired him and, as a clansman, treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 既擢第，補渝州南平令，理甚有聲。

translations.literal: After he passed the examination he was appointed Nanping district magistrate in Yuzhou, and his governance had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the civil examination he was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Yuzhou and earned a strong reputation for governance.

sentences.zh: 至德中，河東節度王思禮奏為參謀，累授大理司直、監察殿中侍御史、節度判官。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era Hedong military commissioner Wang Sili memorialized him as staff adviser; he was repeatedly appointed Directing Censor in the Court of Judicial Review, Supervisory Palace Attending Censor, and military-commission aide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide reign Wang Sili, military commissioner of Hedong, recommended him as staff adviser. He rose through posts as directing censor in the Court of Judicial Review, supervisory palace attending censor, and military commission aide.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，入為金部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he entered court as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Metals section.
translations.idiomatic: In 762 he entered central office as vice director in the ministry of revenue's metals section.

sentences.zh: 尋授侍御史、迥紇糧料使，改檢校職方員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attending Censor and Uyghur grain-supply commissioner, and changed to Provisional Vice Director in the Ministry of War's Offices section.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made attending censor and commissioner for Uyghur grain supplies, then provisional vice director in the ministry of war's offices section.

sentences.zh: 充使檢校郎官，自少遊始也。

translations.literal: Serving as envoy with provisional review of officials began with Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of appointing an envoy with provisional authority to review officials began with Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 明年，仆固懷恩奏為河北副元帥判官、兵部郎中、兼侍御史。

translations.literal: The next year Pugu Huai'en memorialized him as aide to the Hebei deputy commander-in-chief, Director in the Ministry of War, and concurrently Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Pugu Huai'en appointed him aide to the Hebei deputy commander-in-chief, director in the ministry of war, and attending censor.

sentences.zh: 遷晉州刺史，改同州刺史，未視事，又歷晉、鄭二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jinzhou prefect, changed to Tongzhou prefect, before taking office again served in turn as Jin and Zheng prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Jinzhou, then Tongzhou, and before taking the latter post served again as prefect of Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 少遊為理，長於權變，時推幹濟，然厚斂財貨，交結權幸，以是頻獲遷擢。

translations.literal: Shaoyou in governance was skilled at expedient adaptation; his time praised his practical ability, yet he heavily levied wealth and goods and cultivated connections with the powerful and favored, and thereby frequently gained promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In administration Shaoyou was resourceful and widely praised for practical ability, yet he levied heavy taxes, cultivated powerful patrons, and thereby won frequent promotions.

sentences.zh: 無幾，澤潞節度使李抱玉表為副使、御史中丞、陳鄭二州留後。

translations.literal: Before long Zelu military commissioner Li Baoyu memorialized him as deputy commissioner, Censor-in-Chief, and acting governor of Chen and Zheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Baoyu, military commissioner of Zelu, recommended him as deputy commissioner, censor-in-chief, and acting governor of Chen and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，抱玉又奏為隴右行軍司馬，拜檢校左庶子，依前兼中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai Baoyu again memorialized him as campaign marshal of Longyou, appointing him Provisional Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, continuing as before as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 766 Li Baoyu recommended him as campaign marshal of Longyou and provisional left guardian of the heir apparent, while retaining the post of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其年，除桂州刺史、桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: That year he was made Guizhou prefect and Guiguan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of the Guiguan circuit.

sentences.zh: 少遊以嶺僥遐遠，欲規求近郡。

translations.literal: Shaoyou because the Ling region was remote and distant wished to scheme for a nearer commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou regarded the Lingnan post as too remote and schemed to obtain a nearer prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時中官董秀掌樞密用事，少遊乃宿於其裏，候其下直，際晚謁之，從容曰：「七郎家中人數幾何？

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Dong Xiu controlled secret matters and wielded power; Shaoyou lodged in his lane, waited until he came off duty, and at dusk called on him, saying at ease: "Seventh Brother, how many people are in your household?"
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Dong Xiu then controlled secret affairs. Shaoyou lodged near his residence, waited until he came off duty, and called at dusk, asking casually, "Seventh Brother, how large is your household?"

sentences.zh: 每月所費復幾何？

translations.literal: How much do you spend each month?
translations.idiomatic: And what are your monthly expenses?

sentences.zh: 」秀曰：「久忝近職，家累甚重，又屬時物騰貴，一月過千餘貫。

translations.literal: " Xiu said: "For long I have been honored with a post near the throne; family burdens are very heavy, and moreover goods are rising in price—more than a thousand strings a month."
translations.idiomatic: Dong replied, "I have long held a post close to the throne, my household is large, and prices are rising—more than a thousand strings of cash each month."

sentences.zh: 」少遊曰：「據此之費，俸錢不足支數日，其餘常須數求外人，方可取濟。

translations.literal: " Shaoyou said: "According to these expenses, salary money is insufficient to last several days; the rest must constantly be sought several times from outsiders before one can make ends meet."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou said, "At that rate your salary would last only a few days; you must constantly seek help from outsiders to make ends meet."

sentences.zh: 倘有輸誠供億者，但留心庇覆之，固易為力耳。

translations.literal: If someone offers sincere support and supplies, you need only take care to shelter him—it is indeed easy to exert effort.
translations.idiomatic: If someone offers loyal support, you need only protect him—it would be easy enough to arrange.

sentences.zh: 少遊雖不才，請以一身獨供七郎之費，每歲請獻錢五萬貫。

translations.literal: Though Shaoyou lacks talent, he requests to supply Seventh Brother's expenses alone by himself, offering fifty thousand strings of cash each year.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I beg to cover all your household expenses myself—fifty thousand strings of cash each year.

sentences.zh: 今見有大半，請即受納，餘到官續送。

translations.literal: Now more than half is visible; please accept it at once, and the remainder will be sent continuously after I take office.
translations.idiomatic: I have more than half ready now—please accept it at once; the rest I will send after I take up my post.

sentences.zh: 免貴人勞慮，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Spare the noble person labor and worry—is that not also acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Would that not spare you worry and trouble?

sentences.zh: 」秀既逾於始望，欣愜頗甚，因與之厚相結。

translations.literal: " Xiu, having exceeded his initial hopes, was greatly pleased and satisfied, and therefore formed a deep bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong, far exceeding his expectations, was delighted and formed a close bond with him.

sentences.zh: 少遊言訖，泣曰：「南方炎瘴，深愴違辭，但恐不生還再睹顏色矣。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou finished speaking he wept and said: "The south has blazing miasma; I am deeply grieved to part from you, and fear I may not return alive to see your face again."
translations.idiomatic: When he finished, Shaoyou wept and said, "The southern heat and miasma grieve me as I take leave—I fear I may never return alive to see you again."

sentences.zh: 」秀遽曰：「中丞美才，不當遠官，請從容旬日，冀竭蹇分。

translations.literal: " Xiu said hastily: "The Vice Commissioner has fine talent and should not take a distant post; please wait at ease for ten days, hoping to exhaust my feeble share of effort."
translations.idiomatic: Dong said quickly, "Your talent should not be sent so far—wait ten days, and I will do all I can."

sentences.zh: 」時少遊又已納賄於元載子仲武矣。

translations.literal: " At that time Shaoyou had also already paid bribes to Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shaoyou had also bribed Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 秀、載內外引薦，數日，拜宣州刺史、宣歙池都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Xiu and Zai recommended him inside and outside; within days he was appointed Xuanzhou prefect and overall training-and-observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: With recommendations from Dong within the palace and Yuan Zai without, within days he was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou and overall training-and-observation commissioner of the Xuan-She-Chi circuit.

sentences.zh: 大歷五年，改越州刺史、兼御史大夫、浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali he was changed to Yuezhou prefect, concurrently Chief Censor, and Zhedong observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 770 he was transferred to prefect of Yuezhou, chief censor, and observation commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 八年遷揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Senior Administrator of Yangzhou Superior Prefecture and Huainan military and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 773 he became senior administrator of Yangzhou and military and observation commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 仍加銀青光祿大夫，封潁川縣開國子。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master of the Palace and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yingchuan county.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made silver-green glory grand master of the palace and enfeoffed as viscount of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 所在悉心綏輯，而多以任數為政，好行小惠，胥吏得職，人亦獲安。

translations.literal: Wherever he was he devoted himself to soothing and ordering, yet mostly governed by expedient calculation, liking to grant small favors; clerks obtained their duties and the people also gained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he worked diligently to restore order, yet governed chiefly by calculation and small favors; clerks kept their posts and the people found a measure of peace.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷多事。

translations.literal: When the court had many affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the court faced many crises,

sentences.zh: 奏請本道兩稅錢千增二百。

translations.literal: he memorialized requesting that within his circuit the two-tax money per thousand be increased by two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: he memorialized to raise the circuit's two-tax levy by two hundred cash per thousand.

sentences.zh: 因詔諸道悉如淮南，鹽每一斗更加一百文。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered all circuits to follow Huainan alike, adding one hundred cash to each dou of salt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered every circuit to follow Huainan's example, adding one hundred cash per dou of salt.

sentences.zh: 少遊十餘年間，三總大籓，皆天下殷厚處也。

translations.literal: Within more than ten years Shaoyou thrice headed great frontier commands, all places of wealth and abundance under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than ten years Shaoyou held three of the empire's wealthiest great commands.

sentences.zh: 以故征求貿易，且無虛日，斂積財寶，累巨億萬，多賂遺權貴，視文雅清流之士，蔑如也。

translations.literal: Therefore he levied and sought trade without a single idle day, amassed treasures amounting to hundreds of millions, gave many bribes to the powerful and favored, and regarded refined, pure-stream scholars with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: He taxed and traded without pause, amassed wealth in the hundreds of millions, lavished bribes on the powerful, and held refined scholars in contempt.

sentences.zh: 初結元載，每年饋金帛約十萬貫，又多納賂於用事中官駱奉先、劉清潭、吳承倩等，由是美聲達於中禁。

translations.literal: At first he bonded with Yuan Zai, each year presenting gold and silks of about one hundred thousand strings, and also paid many bribes to influential eunuchs Luo Fengxian, Liu Qingtan, Wu Chengqian, and others; thereby his fine reputation reached the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He first cultivated Yuan Zai with annual gifts of some one hundred thousand strings in gold and silk, and bribed influential eunuchs such as Luo Fengxian, Liu Qingtan, and Wu Chengqian, so that his reputation reached the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後見元載在相位年深，以過犯漸見疑忌，少遊亦稍疏之。

translations.literal: Later seeing Yuan Zai long in the chancellorship and gradually suspected for faults, Shaoyou also grew somewhat distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Yuan Zai's long tenure bred suspicion of his misconduct, Shaoyou grew somewhat distant.

sentences.zh: 無何，載子伯和貶官揚州，少遊外與之交結，而陰使人伺其過失，密以上聞。

translations.literal: Before long Zai's son Bohe was demoted to an office in Yangzhou; Shaoyou outwardly befriended him while secretly sending men to watch for his faults and report them upward in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Zai's son Bohe was demoted to Yangzhou. Shaoyou befriended him openly while secretly having his faults reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 代宗以為忠，待之益厚。

translations.literal: Daizong regarded this as loyalty and treated him still more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong took this as proof of loyalty and treated him still more favorably.

sentences.zh: 上即位，累加檢校禮部、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he was repeatedly made Provisional Minister of Rites and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne he was repeatedly made provisional minister of rites and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，李納反叛，少遊以師收徐、海等州，尋棄之，退軍盱眙。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong Li Na rebelled; Shaoyou with his army recovered Xu, Hai, and other prefectures, then soon abandoned them and withdrew the army to Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In 782, when Li Na rebelled, Shaoyou briefly recovered Xu, Hai, and other prefectures, then abandoned them and withdrew to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 又加檢校左僕射，賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Provisional Left Vice Director and granted three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made provisional left vice director and granted three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 其年，就加同平章事。

translations.literal: That year he was promptly made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made associate grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 關播嘗為少遊賓僚，盧杞早年與之同在仆固懷恩使府，故驟加其官秩。

translations.literal: Guan Bo had once been Shaoyou's guest staff; Lu Qi in early years had been with him together in Pugu Huai'en's mission office, and therefore his rank was suddenly raised.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo had once been on his staff, and Lu Qi had served with him in Pugu Huai'en's mission office in earlier years—hence his rapid promotions.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，駕幸奉天，度支汴東兩稅使包佶在揚州，尚未知也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year the imperial carriage went to Fengtian; Revenue Commissioner for Bian and East Bao Ji was in Yangzhou and did not yet know of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 783 the emperor withdrew to Fengtian. Bao Ji, commissioner for Bian and eastern two-tax revenues, was in Yangzhou and had not yet heard the news.

sentences.zh: 佶判官崔沅遽報少遊，佶時所總賦稅錢帛約八百萬貫在焉，少遊意以為賊據京師，未即收復，遂脅取其財物。

translations.literal: Ji's aide Cui Yuan hastily reported to Shaoyou; the tax money and silks Ji then oversaw amounted to about eight million strings; Shaoyou thought rebels held the capital and it would not soon be recovered, and therefore coerced and seized his goods.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's aide Cui Yuan hurried to inform Shaoyou. Ji was overseeing some eight million strings in tax revenues. Shaoyou assumed rebels held the capital and would not soon be driven out, and seized the funds by force.

sentences.zh: 先使判官崔就佶強索其納給文歷，並請供二百萬貫錢物以助軍費，佶答曰：「所用財帛，須承敕命。

translations.literal: First he sent aide Cui to Ji to forcibly demand his payment documents, and also requested supply of two million strings in money and goods to aid military expenses; Ji replied: "Funds and silks used must await imperial edict."
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Cui to demand Ji's payment records and request two million strings for military expenses. Ji replied, "Such funds require an imperial order."

sentences.zh: 」未與之。

translations.literal: " and did not give them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 勃然曰：「中丞若得，為劉長卿；

translations.literal: He said in anger: "If the Vice Commissioner obtains them, he will be like Liu Changqing;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou flared up and said, "If you comply, you will fare like Liu Changqing;

sentences.zh: 不爾，為崔眾矣。

translations.literal: if not, he will be like Cui Zhong."
translations.idiomatic: if not, like Cui Zhong."

sentences.zh: 」長卿嘗任租庸使，為吳仲孺所困，崔眾供軍吝財，為光弼所殺，故言及之，佶大懼，不敢固護，財帛將轉輸入京師者，悉為少遊奪之。

translations.literal: " Changqing had once served as Commissioner of Tax and Corvée and was trapped by Wu Zhongru; Cui Zhong was stingy with funds for supplying the army and was killed by Guo Guangbi—hence he mentioned them. Ji was greatly afraid and did not dare firmly protect them; all wealth and silks about to be transported to the capital were seized by Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Liu Changqing, once trapped while serving as tax commissioner, and Cui Zhong, killed by Guo Guangbi for withholding army funds. Ji was terrified and yielded; all goods bound for the capital were seized.

sentences.zh: 佶自謁，少遊止焉，長揖而遣，既懼禍，奔往白沙。

translations.literal: Ji came to call on him in person; Shaoyou detained him, gave a long bow and sent him off; fearing disaster, he fled to Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: Ji came in person, but Shaoyou detained him briefly, bowed, and dismissed him. Fearing worse, Ji fled to Baisha.

sentences.zh: 少遊又遣判官房孺復召之，佶愈懼，托以巡檢，因急棹過江，妻子伏案牘中。

translations.literal: Shaoyou again sent aide Fang Rufu to summon him; Ji grew still more afraid, pleaded inspection duties, and urgently rowed across the river, his wife and children hiding among the documents.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou sent another aide to summon him. Ji, still more afraid, claimed inspection duties, crossed the river in haste, and hid his wife and children among the document cases.

sentences.zh: 至上元，復為韓滉所拘留。

translations.literal: Reaching Shangyuan he was again detained by Han Huang.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangyuan he was detained again by Han Huang.

sentences.zh: 佶先有兵三千，守禦財貨，令高越、元甫將焉，少遊盡奪之。

translations.literal: Ji had earlier had three thousand troops guarding the wealth, commanded by Gao Yue and Yuan Fu; Shaoyou seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's three thousand troops guarding the treasury under Gao Yue and Yuan Fu were all seized by Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 隨佶渡江者，又為韓滉所留，佶但領胥吏往江、鄂等州。

translations.literal: Those who crossed the river with Ji were again held by Han Huang; Ji led only clerks to Jiang, E, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Those who crossed with him were detained by Han Huang as well, and Ji proceeded with only clerks to Jiang, E, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 佶於彈丸中置表，以少遊脅取財帛事。

translations.literal: Ji placed a memorial inside a pellet, reporting Shaoyou's coercion and seizure of wealth and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Ji concealed a memorial in a pellet reporting Shaoyou's seizure of the funds.

sentences.zh: 會少遊使繼至，上問曰：「少遊取包佶財帛，有之乎？

translations.literal: When Shaoyou's envoy next arrived, the emperor asked: "Did Shaoyou take Bao Ji's wealth and silks?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou's envoy next arrived, the emperor asked, "Did Shaoyou seize Bao Ji's funds?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣發揚州後，非所知也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "After your servant left Yangzhou, it was not within his knowledge."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy replied, "After I left Yangzhou, I do not know."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「少遊國之守臣，或防他盜，供費軍旅，收亦何傷。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Shaoyou is a guardian minister of the state; perhaps guarding against other bandits and supplying military expenses—what harm in seizing them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shaoyou is a guardian of the realm; if he seized funds to supply the army or guard against other threats, what harm was done?"

sentences.zh: 」時方隅阻絕，國命未振，遠近聞之大驚，鹹以聖情達於變通，明見萬里。

translations.literal: " At that time the regions were cut off and the state's mandate not yet restored; near and far hearing this were greatly startled, all deeming the sage heart reached expedient adaptation and saw clearly ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: With communications cut off and the dynasty still unsteady, all who heard this marveled at the emperor's pragmatic judgment and far-reaching vision.

sentences.zh: 少遊後聞之，乃安。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou later heard of it he was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou later heard this he was greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 及李希烈陷汴州，聲言欲襲江淮。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou he declared he would strike the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou he announced an intended strike on the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 少遊懼，乃使參謀溫述由壽州送款於希烈曰：「濠、壽、舒、廬，尋令罷壘，韜戈卷甲，佇候指揮。

translations.literal: Shaoyou was afraid and sent staff adviser Wen Shu from Shouzhou to offer submission to Xilie, saying: "Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu will soon be ordered to dismantle fortifications, sheath weapons and roll up armor, and await your command."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Shaoyou sent his adviser Wen Shu from Shouzhou to submit to Xilie, pledging to dismantle fortifications in Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu and await his orders.

sentences.zh: 」少遊又遣巡官趙詵於鄆州結李納。

translations.literal: " Shaoyou also sent touring officer Zhao Shen to Yanzhou to ally with Li Na.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent touring officer Zhao Shen to Yanzhou to ally with Li Na.

sentences.zh: 其年，希烈僭號，遣其將楊豐賫偽赦書赴揚州，至壽州，為刺史張建封候騎所得，建封對中使二人及少遊判官許子瑞廷責豐而斬之。

translations.literal: That year Xilie usurped a title and sent his general Yang Feng bearing a false amnesty to Yangzhou; reaching Shouzhou he was seized by prefect Zhang Jianfeng's scouting riders; Jianfeng in court rebuked Feng before two palace envoys and Shaoyou's aide Xu Zirui and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xilie declared himself emperor and sent Yang Feng with a false amnesty to Yangzhou. At Shouzhou, Zhang Jianfeng's scouts seized him, and in open court Zhang rebuked and beheaded him before palace envoys and Shaoyou's aide Xu Zirui.

sentences.zh: 希烈聞之大怒，即署其大將杜少誠為偽僕射、淮南節度，令先平壽州，後取廣陵。

translations.literal: Xilie heard this and was greatly enraged; he immediately appointed his great general Du Shaocheng false Vice Director and Huainan military commissioner, ordering him first to pacify Shouzhou and afterward take Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was furious and appointed his general Du Shaocheng false vice director and Huainan military commissioner, ordering him first to take Shouzhou and then Guangling.

sentences.zh: 建封於霍丘堅柵，嚴加守禁，少誠竟不能進。

translations.literal: Jianfeng at Huoqiu built stout palisades and strictly enforced guard prohibitions; Shaocheng in the end could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng fortified Huoqiu and held it so firmly that Du Shaocheng could not advance.

sentences.zh: 後包佶入朝，具奏少遊奪財賦事狀，少遊大懼，乃上表，以所取包佶財貨，皆是供軍急用，今請據數卻納。

translations.literal: Later Bao Ji entered court and fully reported the circumstances of Shaoyou's seizure of revenues; Shaoyou was greatly afraid and submitted a memorial that the goods taken from Bao Ji were all for urgent military supply and he now requested to return them according to the tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao Ji reached court and reported the seizure in full, Shaoyou was terrified and memorialized that the funds had been taken for urgent military needs and offered to repay the full amount.

sentences.zh: 既而州府殘破，無以上填，乃與腹心孔目官等設法重稅管內百姓以供之。

translations.literal: Soon the prefecture and offices were ravaged and there was no means to make up the amount; he therefore with trusted ledger clerks devised methods to heavily tax the people within his jurisdiction to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: But his circuit lay in ruins and could not cover the sum, so he and his trusted clerks imposed heavy new taxes on the people to pay it back.

sentences.zh: 無何，劉洽收汴州，得希烈偽起居註「某月日陳少遊上表歸順。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Qia recovered Bianzhou and obtained Xilie's false court diary: "On such-and-such month and day Chen Shaoyou submitted a memorial of submission."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Qia recovered Bianzhou and found in Xilie's forged court diary an entry dated to Shaoyou's submission.

sentences.zh: 」少遊聞之，慚惶發疾，數日而卒，年六十一，贈太尉，賻布帛，葬祭如常儀。

translations.literal: " When Shaoyou heard of it he was ashamed and alarmed, fell ill, and died within days, at age sixty-one; he was posthumously made Grand Commandant, with condolence silks, and burial and sacrifice according to ordinary rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou learned of this he fell ill with shame and died within days at sixty-one. He was posthumously honored as grand commandant, with state condolence gifts and ordinary funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 盧鸑，幽州范陽人也，貞觀中工部侍郎義恭玄孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Yue was a man of Fanyang in Youzhou, the great-great-grandson of Yigong, Vice Minister of Works in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yue came from Fanyang in Youzhou and was the great-great-grandson of Yigong, vice minister of works under Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 父子騫，潁王府諮議參軍，以鸑贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: His father Ziqian was Staff Adviser to the Prince of Ying's household; because of Yue he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziqian had been staff adviser to the Prince of Ying's household and was posthumously honored as vice director of the Secretariat through Yue's promotions.

sentences.zh: 鸑少以門廕入仕，在職以幹局稱。

translations.literal: Yue in youth entered office through hereditary privilege and in service was known for practical competence.
translations.idiomatic: Yue entered office through hereditary privilege and was known for practical administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 累授閬州錄事參軍、監察殿中御史、侍御史、金州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Records Officer in Langzhou, Supervisory Palace Censor, Attending Censor, and Jinzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts as records officer in Langzhou, supervisory palace censor, attending censor, and prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊炎遇之頗厚，召入左司郎中、京兆少尹，遷大尹。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yang Yan treated him quite generously, summoned him as Director in the Left Secretariat, Junior Magistrate of the Capital District, and transferred him to Chief Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Yang Yan favored him, recalled him as director in the left secretariat and junior magistrate of the capital district, then chief magistrate.

sentences.zh: 鸑無術學，善事權要，為政苛躁。

translations.literal: Yue had no scholarly learning, was skilled at serving the powerful and favored, and in government was harsh and rash.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had no scholarly training, curried favor with the powerful, and governed harshly and impatiently.

sentences.zh: 盧杞甚惡之，諷有司彈奏，坐貶撫州司馬同正，改饒州刺史，遷福州刺史、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: Lu Qi greatly hated him, prompted the relevant offices to impeach him, and he was demoted to Fuzhou Vice Military Administrator with the same-rank stipend, changed to Raozhou prefect, and transferred to Fuzhou prefect and Fujian observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi detested him, had him impeached, and demoted him to vice military administrator of Fuzhou on reduced stipend, then made him prefect of Raozhou and later Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年七月，以疾終。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyuan he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the seventh month of 786.

sentences.zh: 裴谞，字士明，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Pei Xu, style name Shiming, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xu, whose courtesy name was Shiming, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父寬，禮部尚書，有重名於開元、天寶間。

translations.literal: His father Kuan was Minister of Rites and had a weighty reputation in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuan had served as minister of rites and enjoyed great renown during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns.

sentences.zh: 谞少舉明經，補河南府參軍，通達簡率，不好苛細。

translations.literal: Xu in youth passed the Mingjing examination, was appointed Henan prefectural aide, was open and direct in manner, and did not like petty exactness.
translations.idiomatic: Xu passed the mingjing examination in youth, was appointed an aide in the Henan prefectural office, and was open, direct, and impatient with petty detail.

sentences.zh: 積官至京兆倉曹，丁父喪，居東都。

translations.literal: He accumulated offices to Capital District Granary Officer, entered mourning for his father, and resided in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to granary officer in the capital district, then retired to the eastern capital upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 是時，安祿山盜陷二京，東都收復，遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: At that time An Lushan rebelliously captured the two capitals; when the Eastern Capital was recovered he was transferred to Heir Apparent Admonisher.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan seized the two capitals and the eastern capital was later recovered, he was appointed admonisher to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 無幾，虢王巨奏署侍御史、襄鄧營田判官，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Before long Prince of Guo Ju memorialized his appointment as Attending Censor and Xiang-Deng agricultural colony aide, then he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Guo appointed him attending censor and agricultural colony aide for Xiang and Deng, after which he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 東都復為史思明所陷，谞藏匿山谷。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital was again captured by Shi Siming; Xu hid in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern capital fell again to Shi Siming, Xu hid in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 思明嘗為谞父將校，懷舊恩，又素慕谞名，欲必得之，因令捕騎數十跡逐得谞。

translations.literal: Siming had once been a commander under Xu's father and cherished old favor; he had also long admired Xu's name and wished to obtain him at all costs, and therefore ordered several dozen pursuit riders to track and seize Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Siming had once served under Xu's father and, cherishing old ties and long admiring Xu's reputation, sent dozens of riders to hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 思明見之，甚喜，呼為郎君，不名，偽授御史中丞，主擊斷。

translations.literal: When Siming saw him he was very pleased, called him Young Master without using his name, and falsely appointed him Censor-in-Chief in charge of judgments.
translations.idiomatic: Siming was delighted, addressed him respectfully as "young master," and falsely appointed him censor-in-chief in charge of judicial decisions.

sentences.zh: 時思明殘殺宗室，谞陰緩之，全活者數百人。

translations.literal: At that time Siming slaughtered the imperial clan; Xu secretly slowed proceedings, and those wholly saved numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: As Siming slaughtered members of the imperial clan, Xu secretly slowed proceedings and saved hundreds of lives.

sentences.zh: 又嘗疏賊短長以聞，事泄，思明大怒詬罵，僅而免死。

translations.literal: He also once memorialized the rebels' strengths and weaknesses to inform the court; the matter leaked, Siming raged and reviled him, and he barely escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent intelligence on the rebels to the Tang court; when this was discovered Siming raged at him and he barely escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 賊平，除太子中允，遷考功郎中，數召見言事。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was made Heir Apparent Moderator, transferred to Director in the Examination section, and repeatedly summoned to audience to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he was made moderator to the heir apparent, then director in the examination office, and was repeatedly summoned to advise the throne.

sentences.zh: 代宗居陜，谞步懷考功及南曹二印赴行在，上見而謂之曰：「疾風知勁草，果信矣。

translations.literal: When Daizong resided in Shan, Xu walked carrying the Examination and Southern Bureau seals to the mobile court; the emperor saw him and said: "A fierce wind reveals the tough grass—truly believed."
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong was at Shan, Xu walked to the mobile court carrying the seals of the examination and southern personnel offices. The emperor said, "A fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true that proverb is."

sentences.zh: 」將以為御史中丞，為無載所排，為河東道租庸鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: " He was about to be made Censor-in-Chief but was blocked by Yuan Zai and made Commissioner of Tax, Corvée, Salt, and Iron for the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was to be made censor-in-chief, but Yuan Zai blocked the appointment and had him made commissioner of tax, corvée, salt, and iron for the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 時關輔大旱，谞入計，代宗召見便殿，問谞：「榷酤之利，一歲出入幾何？

translations.literal: At that time the Guanzhong region suffered great drought; Xu entered to report accounts; Daizong summoned him in the side hall and asked Xu: "The profit from the liquor monopoly—how much comes in and goes out in a year?"
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought in the Guanzhong region Xu came to report accounts. Daizong received him in a side hall and asked, "What is the annual revenue from the liquor monopoly?"

sentences.zh: 」谞久之不對。

translations.literal: " Xu for a long time did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was silent for a long time.

sentences.zh: 上復問之，對曰：「臣有所思。

translations.literal: The emperor asked again; he replied: "Your servant has something on his mind."
translations.idiomatic: Asked again, he said, "Your servant has been thinking."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何思？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Thinking of what?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "About what?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣自河東來，其間所歷三百里，見農人愁嘆，谷菽未種。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant came from Hedong; along the three hundred li he passed he saw farmers grieving and sighing, grain and beans not yet planted."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Coming from Hedong I passed three hundred li of countryside and saw farmers grieving—grain and beans still unplanted."

sentences.zh: 誠謂陛下軫念，先問人之疾苦，而乃責臣以利。

translations.literal: He truly thought Your Majesty would be concerned and first ask of people's suffering and hardship, yet instead charged your servant about profit.
translations.idiomatic: I thought Your Majesty would first ask about the people's suffering, not press me about profit.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：理國者，仁義而已，何以利為？

translations.literal: Mencius said: Those who order the state have only benevolence and righteousness—why take profit as the basis?
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said that to govern a state one needs benevolence and righteousness—why make profit the first concern?

sentences.zh: 由是未敢即對也。

translations.literal: For this reason he did not dare answer at once.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I did not answer at once.

sentences.zh: 」上前坐曰：「微公言，吾不聞此。

translations.literal: " The emperor came forward and sat, saying: "But for your words, We would not have heard this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose and said, "Without your words I would never have heard this."

sentences.zh: 」拜左司郎中。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Director in the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director in the left secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上時訪以事，執政者忌之，出為虔州刺史，歷饒、廬、亳三州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor often consulted him on affairs; those in power resented him and he was sent out as Qianzhou prefect, then served in turn as prefect of Rao, Lu, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often sought his counsel, but the chief ministers resented him and sent him out as prefect of Qianzhou, then Rao, Lu, and Bo in succession.

sentences.zh: 入為右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right General of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned as general of the right golden crow guard.

sentences.zh: 建中初，上以刑名理天下，百吏震悚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong the emperor governed All Under Heaven by penal law; the hundred officials trembled in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign the emperor governed through strict penal law, and officials throughout the bureaucracy trembled.

sentences.zh: 時十月禁屠殺，以甫近山陵，禁益嚴。

translations.literal: At that time in the tenth month slaughter was forbidden; because it was just after the imperial tombs the prohibition was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month slaughter was forbidden, and the ban was especially strict as the court was near the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 尚父、汾陽王郭子儀隸人殺羊以入，門者覺之，谞列奏狀，上以為不畏強禦，累遣宣諭。

translations.literal: The Esteemed Father, Prince of Fenyang Guo Ziyi, had a household servant kill a sheep to bring in; the gate guards detected it; Xu submitted a detailed memorial, and the emperor regarded it as not fearing the powerful and repeatedly sent commendations.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, prince of Fenyang, had a servant bring in a slaughtered sheep in violation of the ban. Xu reported it in full. The emperor praised his fearlessness before the powerful and repeatedly commended him.

sentences.zh: 或謂谞曰：「郭公有社稷功，豈不為蓋之？

translations.literal: Someone said to Xu: "The Duke has merit for the altars of state—would you not cover it for him?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him, "The prince saved the dynasty—why not cover this for him?"

sentences.zh: 」谞笑曰：「非爾所解。

translations.literal: " Xu smiled and said: "That is not what you understand."
translations.idiomatic: Xu smiled and said, "You would not understand."

sentences.zh: 且郭公威權太盛，上新即位，必謂黨附者眾。

translations.literal: Moreover the Duke's authority and power are too great; the emperor has newly taken the throne and is sure to think those who attach to him are many.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's power is too great, and a newly enthroned emperor is bound to suspect a vast following.

sentences.zh: 今發其細過，以明不弄權耳。

translations.literal: Now to expose his small fault is to make clear he does not manipulate power.
translations.idiomatic: By exposing a small fault I show that he does not abuse his power.

sentences.zh: 吾上以盡事君之道，下以安大臣，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Above I thereby fulfill the way of serving the ruler; below I thereby reassure a great minister—is that not also acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Thus I serve the emperor faithfully above and reassure a great minister below—is that not fitting?

sentences.zh: 」時於朝堂別置三司以決庶獄，辯爭者輒擊登聞鼓，谞上疏曰：「夫諫豉謗木之設，所以達幽枉，延直言。

translations.literal: " At that time three offices were separately established in the court hall to decide common cases; disputants would strike the Petition-to-the-Throne drum; Xu submitted a memorial saying: "The setting up of the remonstrance drum and the slander post is to reach hidden wrongs and extend straight speech."
translations.idiomatic: Separate tribunals had been set up in the hall, and litigants would strike the petition drum. Xu memorialized: "The remonstrance drum and slander post were established to reach hidden wrongs and encourage frank speech."

sentences.zh: 今輕猾之人，援桴鳴鼓，始動天聽，竟因纖微。

translations.literal: Now frivolous and cunning people take the mallet and sound the drum, at first moving Heaven's hearing, yet in the end because of trifles.
translations.idiomatic: Now frivolous troublemakers strike the drum over trifles and reach the emperor's ear with petty grievances.

sentences.zh: 若然者，安用吏理乎！

translations.literal: If it is so, what use are officials in governance!
translations.idiomatic: If that is allowed, what need is there for regular officials?

sentences.zh: 」上然之，悉歸有司。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved it and returned all cases to the regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and returned all such cases to the regular offices.

sentences.zh: 谞以法吏舞文，多挾宿怨，因獻《獄官箴》以諷。

translations.literal: Xu because legal clerks manipulated texts and often carried old resentments therefore presented the Admonition for Prison Officials as satire.
translations.idiomatic: Because legal clerks twisted the law and often pursued old grudges, Xu submitted his Admonition for Prison Officials as an indirect critique.

sentences.zh: 無何，坐所善僧抵法，貶閬州司馬。

translations.literal: Before long, because a monk he favored violated the law, he was demoted to Langzhou Vice Military Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted to vice military administrator of Langzhou when a monk he favored ran afoul of the law.

sentences.zh: 征為右庶子，改千牛上將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent and changed to Senior General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as right guardian of the heir apparent, then made senior general of the thousand-ox guard.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃入寇，尋拜吏部侍郎、兼御史大夫，為吐蕃使，不行。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans invaded he was soon appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently Chief Censor, made envoy to the Tibetans, but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet invaded he was soon made vice minister of personnel and chief censor and appointed envoy to Tibet, but did not go.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉太子賓客、兵部侍郎、河南尹、東都副留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Heir Apparent Guest, Vice Minister of War, Henan Magistrate, and Eastern Capital Deputy Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became guest of the heir apparent, vice minister of war, magistrate of Henan, and deputy guardian of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 谞自河南凡五代為官，入視事，未嘗當正處，不鞫認於贓罪，以寬厚和易為理。

translations.literal: Xu's family in Henan had served as officials for five generations; when he entered to conduct affairs he never sat in the main seat, did not interrogate confessions in cases of corruption, and governed by generous breadth and mild ease.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations of Xu's family had served in Henan. When he took office he never sat in the main seat of judgment, avoided pressing confessions in corruption cases, and governed with generous mildness.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年十一月，以疾終，年七十五，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at age seventy-five and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the eleventh month of 793 at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously honored as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李揆發言沃心，幸遇明主；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Li Kui's words enriched the heart and he fortunately met an enlightened ruler;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Li Kui spoke words that enriched the ruler's mind and was fortunate to serve an enlightened sovereign;

sentences.zh: 蔽賢固位，終非令人。

translations.literal: he obscured worthies and held his position fast, and in the end was not a man to be approved.
translations.idiomatic: yet he blocked the worthy and clung to power, and in the end was not a man to admire.

sentences.zh: 少遊逐勢利隨時，盧惎事權要巧宦，察言觀行，皆無可稱。

translations.literal: Shaoyou pursued power and profit according to the times; Lu Yue served the powerful and favored with crafty office-seeking—in examining words and observing conduct, none merit praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou chased power and profit as times changed, and Lu Yue curried favor with the mighty through crafty office-seeking—judged by word and deed, neither deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 涵節行著聞，谞和易為理，庶幾近仁也。

translations.literal: Han's integrity and conduct were renowned; Xu's mild ease in governance were perhaps nearly benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Han's integrity was well known, and Xu's mild governance approached something like benevolence.

sentences.zh: 贊曰李、陳、盧鸑，言行非真。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Li, Chen, and Lu Yue—in word and conduct were not true.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Li, Chen, and Lu Yue were false in word and deed.

sentences.zh: 涵、谞和易，庶乎近仁。

translations.literal: Han and Xu were mild and easy, perhaps nearly benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Xu were mild in manner, perhaps approaching benevolence.
